chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Detroit's big bands and the Dixieland repertoire
summary: Detroit had twelve-piece bands led by men like Bart Howard, while Wooding's combination played Margie and St. Louis Blues.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I see. Now, before we leave Detroit, I just wanted to ask you what was going on in Detroit at that time, musically?

Well, they had four or five great bands. One fellow that had a great band was named Bart Howard. Now, they had large bands there. They had bands of 12 pieces, and like that. I don't think there was any larger than
that. There was another fellow that had a band there, but I can't think of the name, you know? It's been quite a many years.
See, but they had some nice bands out there.
But we had a Dixieland combination, see. And we stood up there with men like Elma Chambers and Jimmy Harrison, and I could play fairly good then, you know? And we were doing all right.
So you were still playing things like "Margie" and some of the --
The pop tunes of the days.
Yeah, well most of the things were. And then we used such numbers as "St. Louis Blues" and things like that, you know.
